data.expected_signal: any nonzero mismatch count confirms the claim; zero mismatches over exhaustive N sweep plus extremes rebuts it

json_result.metric: exact torch.equal int64 vs sequential reference

evidence.summary: Exact int64 comparison against the sequential reference (torch.equal, tolerance 0) over N=1..32 sweeps, extreme int16 values, and adversarial all-ones amplification inputs: 38 of 143 tests mismatched. Failures begin at N=25 (chunks=4, padded=4) with max absolute differences up to ~1.5e6, far beyond any rounding artifact — the exact-arithmetic contract (tolerance 0) is violated for legal inputs.

rationale: The kernel uses a hand-written two-phase tree scan (_exclusive_chunks) over chunk summaries plus an associative_scan within 8-step chunks; the exclusive-prefix propagation loop and the padding of chunk counts to a power of two are exactly the kinds of logic that can be off-by-one at chunk boundaries or on short rows.

scope_evidence.summary: Every combination of legal matrix, bias and initial values is allowed; 1<=B<=64 and 1<=N<=32; every output element must equal the mathematical target exactly with absolute tolerance 0.

scope_rationale: The contract requires exact integer output for EVERY legal input in B in [1,64], N in [1,32], so any input in that domain producing a wrong output element violates the contract.
statement: The Triton chunked scan implementation produces output that differs from the exact sequential affine recurrence for some legal input in the declared domain (B in [1,64], N in [1,32], matrix entries in {-1,0,1}, any int16 bias/initial).
